text:
Ben Kindel is 19, in his second NHL season, and already playing 17:26 a night for a Penguins team that badly needs its young players to grow up fast. His line reads nine points in 17 games, which looks like a modest step. The number underneath it says he deserves more.

Pittsburgh has scored 12.3 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Kindel on the ice, one of the largest gaps in the league, and that has quietly taken assists off his total. His own finishing is about where it should be (four goals on 4.56 expected goals, a measure of chance quality), so this isn't a shooter in a slump; it's the shots around him not going in. The fair worry is that his individual chances have dipped from last season's rate, and the Penguins are slightly underwater at five-on-five with him out there. What he brings is puck carrying: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him entering the zone with possession on 56% of his tries last season. His power-play goal in the shootout win in San Jose was a reminder of the ceiling. The points should catch up to the play.
